## Observation

Ticket frank-rocky-rat (d52f-823f-894e-499a) carries a `caused_by` LINK event (uuid ceae9de7-8992-47c2-855c-60825331adc3, provenance `explicit`) whose `target_id` is the literal string `6ed2`. That quad matches 2 tickets (6ed2-1e12-0780-4efd, 6ed2-24e5-6985-4faa), so the edge points at no ticket.

`_resolve_caused_by_culprit` in `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` returns `resolve_ticket_id(caused_by.strip(), tracker) or caused_by.strip()`. When the `--caused-by` value is ambiguous or unknown, the raw string is written as the edge target. `_apply_caused_by` also removes the existing `caused_by` edges before writing it, so a typo can replace a valid attribution with a dangling one.

## Impact

The escaped-defect metrics read this edge as an explicit, proven attribution to a ticket that does not exist. Every replay of the source ticket also printed `Error: Ambiguous prefix` until the reducer was quieted (sourish-blonde-blueshark).

## Not yet checked

Whether `rebar link` refuses an ambiguous target the same way, and whether other ticket events hold raw non-canonical targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A close with `--caused-by` that does not resolve to exactly 1 ticket writes no `caused_by` edge and leaves existing edges in place, with a visible warning; a test drives an ambiguous 4-hex value.
- [ ] The dangling `caused_by` edge on frank-rocky-rat is corrected or reported to the operator.
compiled_state.title: A close with an unresolvable --caused-by stores the raw string as the caused_by target
